Run a development server under `hot-reload`. Use `--watch` to restart the server when files change,
even after it crashes.
Requires PHP 8.6 on Unix with ext-pcntl.

```sh
composer require --dev thesis/hot-reload:^0.5
vendor/bin/hot-reload --watch server.php --watch src -- php server.php
```

Pass `--watch` once per file or directory to monitor. The paths must exist when the command starts. The watcher
checks file names and contents every 200 ms. Directories are scanned recursively and symlinks inside them are
skipped. Watch the source and configuration paths you edit to keep the scans small.

Use `--debounce 350ms` or `--debounce=1.5s` to set how long the watcher waits after the last detected edit.
The default is `200ms`. Before requesting a restart the watcher checks for new edits again. Use `--debounce 0`
to request a restart as soon as a poll detects a change. `SIGHUP` always requests a restart immediately.

For an immediate restart request, send `kill -HUP <pid>` to the supervisor PID printed at startup. You can omit
`--watch` to use manual restarts only. The server inherits stdio, so startup errors and application logs appear
in the same terminal. If the server exits, the supervisor reports its exit status and waits for a file change or `SIGHUP`.

`SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` stop the session. On restart or shutdown, the supervisor sends the server `SIGTERM`,
gives it three seconds to exit, and sends `SIGKILL` if it is still running.
The replacement starts after the old server exits. Saves during shutdown go into that same replacement.
